title: {{NAME}} and the Kingdom of Stars
moral: The bravest adventures begin when you dare to look up.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a curious young princess with dark braided hair and warm hazel eyes, wearing a deep blue gown with silver constellation embroidery, a small gold crown, and soft silver slippers — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
Princess {{NAME}} lived in a tall castle at the edge of the kingdom. She had everything a princess could want — a library full of maps, a garden full of roses, and a telescope by her window.

But what she really wanted was to see somewhere new.

"You are a princess," said her tutor. "Princesses do not go wandering."

"Then perhaps," said {{NAME}} thoughtfully, "I shall go at night — when no one is watching."

pages.content:
That very night, {{NAME}} slipped out of her tower just after midnight.

In the castle courtyard, where the moonlight fell at a particular angle on the old fountain, she saw something that had never been there before: a staircase.

It was made of moonbeams — pale silver steps that rose upward and curved out of sight among the clouds.

{{NAME}} placed one foot on the first step. It held. She placed the other. Then she climbed.

pages.content:
At the top of the staircase was a small kingdom — no bigger than {{NAME}}'s bedroom, but absolutely perfect. The houses were made of glass that hummed with their own light. The roads were silver and left trails behind your footsteps.

The people who lived there were no taller than her hand. They had starlight in their hair and voices like tiny bells.

"A visitor!" said the smallest one delightedly. "We haven't had a visitor since — oh, ages!"

"I'm {{NAME}}," she said. "I came to explore."

pages.content:
The star children taught {{NAME}} their greatest secret: a dance that made the stars move.

You had to spin on your left foot, then your right. Clap once, turn, and reach both hands toward the sky. When {{NAME}} did it correctly, two stars overhead swapped places with a little flash.

"Does that mean they can see me?" she asked, looking up.

"Always," said the smallest star child. "They just don't make it obvious."

pages.content:
{{NAME}} climbed down the moonbeam staircase as the sky began to turn from black to the deepest shade of blue.

She slipped back into her tower. She put away her crown and changed into her nightgown and got into bed.

Her tutor would say she had been asleep all night. Her maps wouldn't show where she had been.

But {{NAME}} looked out at the sky through half-closed eyes — and two stars blinked at her.

She smiled, and was asleep before the first bird sang.
